final_answer:
Depth-First Search (DfS) and Breadth-First Search (BfS) are traversal algorithms for graphs. DfS explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, using a stack (or recursion). BfS explores all neighbors at the current depth level before moving to the next, using a queue. 

DfS is memory-efficient for deep graphs but risks infinite loops in cyclic graphs unless tracked. BfS guarantees the shortest path in unweighted graphs but uses more memory for wide graphs. Choose DfS for tasks like cycle detection or maze solving, and BfS for finding the shortest path or when all nodes at a certain depth are needed.
